analytic.title: Response Time Analysis of Parallel Tasks under Global Fixed-priority on Heterogeneous Multi-cores

application.desc: GROBID - A machine learning software for extracting information from scholarly documents

div.p: Heterogeneous multi-core platforms can provide diverse computing power. By using different cores to perform specific workloads, the advantages of heterogeneous multi-cores can be fully utilized to achieve high performance and low power consumption. In this paper, we study the problem of schedulability analysis of parallel directed acyclic graph (DAG) tasks on heterogeneous platforms. The DAG task studied in this paper has particularities. A vertex of a DAG task is only allowed to execute on a specific set of cores. In this paper, we study each DAG task's worst-case response time(WCRT) analysis problem and propose an analyzed method for this particular task model. The new method profoundly looks at the higher priority tasks and combines them with the task graph structure information. Searching for the graph structure is time-consuming, so we propose an efficient analysis method that can be performed in polynomial time. We use simulation experiments to verify the accuracy and time consumption of the proposed algorithm. And the results show that our proposed method can significantly improve the existing method.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: With the development of intelligence, complex systems require rapidly increasing performance and energy efficiency. This phenomenon promotes the development of heterogeneous fusion. To adapt and make full use of heterogeneous platforms, software needs parallel processing.

In real-time systems, The parallel task scheduling problem on heterogeneous platforms is more complex than on homogeneous platforms. In scheduling theory, parallel task scheduling analysis is more complicated than sequential task scheduling analysis. And it has become a hot research topic in real-time scheduling.

A heterogeneous multi-core is more suitable for current market demand than a homogeneous multi-core. Heterogeneous multi-core provides higher performance and lower energy consumption by executing specific program segments through particular processors. For example, the data presented in [4] show that the heterogeneous multi-core platform can improve performance by 21% and save 23%.
At present, many chip manufacturers have produced heterogeneous multi-core products, such as Zynq-7000 [1] and OMAP1/OMAP2 [2], and the Tegra processors [3].

In this paper, we study the scheduling of typed DAG tasks on heterogeneous platforms. These heterogeneous platforms are divided into different types, and we bind each vertex of DAG tasks to execute and can only run on a kind of core. There is less work considering the task model, which is the same as this paper recently. The already known methods are [5] and [6]. [5] has already been compared with [7], which is much more pessimistic due to the end-to-end analysis. And [6] method is much more pessimistic because it considers too many types for one path.

This paper aims to analyze the worst-case response time for DAG tasks. We propose a method to bind the WCRT of DAG tasks to solve the precision problem of the method proposed in [6] (we call this as Base-line). We first extend the busy period analysis method to this typed DAG tasks model and then propose a way to compute the inter-interference for a given path. Finally, we offer an algorithm based on the path abstraction idea to find the WCRT of each typed DAG task in a task set. In this paper, we use simulation experiments to verify the method proposed. Experimental results show that the proposed method can significantly improve the accuracy compared to existing algorithms.

div.head: A. Task Model
div.p: In this paper, we consider a task set

which is executed on a heterogeneous multi-core platform with different types. We use Γ to denote the set of core types (or types for short) and M s (M s ≥ 1) to denote the number of cores of type s for each s ∈ Γ.
div.formula: Task G i (1 ≤ i ≤ n i ) is a typed DAG task, which is denoted by G i = (V i , E i , c i , T i , D i , P i ).
div.p: V i is the set of vertices, and E i is the set of edges. In the rest of this paper, we also use τ i to denote G i . Each vertex v ∈ V i represents a piece of program of G i . We use (u, v) ∈ E i to denote the directed edge from u to v. We use P (v) to denote the type of v. If P (v) = s, then vertex v must be executed on cores of type s. We use c(v) to denote the worstcase execution time (WCET) of vertex v, where v ∈ V i . u is a predecessor of v, and v is a successor of u, if there is an edge (u, v) ∈ E i . u is an ancestor of v and v is a descendant of u, if there is a path in G i from u to v. The set of ancestors, descendants,predecessors, and successors of vertex u are denoted by anc(u), det(u), ped(u) and sus(u), respectively.

To simplify the analysis, this paper assumes that G i has only one source vertex and one sink vertex. If G i has multiple source/sink vertices, one can make it compliant with our model by adding a dummy source/sink vertex (which has zero WCET).

div.head: III. THE NEW WCRT BOUND
div.p: A single vertex DAG task is a particular case of DAG tasks. And the execution behavior of a single vertex DAG task is much simpler than a multi-vertice DAG task(which consists of more than one vertex). In this section, we first propose a method to analyze a single vertex task. And then extend this method to a multi-vertex DAG task. The execution behavior of DAG tasks is complicated. To reduce the complexity, we assume all higher priority tasks are single vertex tasks.

We summarize the above discussion as Algorithm 1, which is a pseudo-code to compute max λ∈G k { R(λ)}. Υ is used to keep the set of tuples at each iteration. Υ initializes with a single tuple of the source vertex of G k . Then the algorithm searches for the successor of the source vertex and generates new tuples. It determines whether the newly generated tuple adds to Υ. If this new tuple is dominated by tuples already in Υ, then this tuple should be deleted. Otherwise, it should be added to Υ(lines 6 to 7). The Algorithm 1 does this searching procedure in a width-first way, so it always chooses a tuple which already finished analyzing its predecessors (line 3). Finally, the searching procedure reaches the sink vertex, and Υ only keeps tuples of the sink vertex. By Lemma 4.1, the largest R among tuples in Υ is the desired max λ∈G { R(λ)}. div.p: In this paper, we use simulation experiments to verify the proposed algorithm's performance from two aspects of precision and efficiency. Note that we only focus on the effects of higher priority tasks on a DAG task. For each task set, we let all single vertex task with higher priority than a DAG task. We use the RM (Rate Monotonic) to set priority for each task set.

First, we set a set of default parameters through prior experience. Then, by adjusting a set of parameters in the default parameters, the effect of this parameter on the experimental data is observed. The default parameter Settings are as follows:

• We set the range of types number is [2,15], the range of the cores number of each type is [2,10]. We randomly choose a value for the number of type and the number of cores for each type, respectively. • The number of single vertex tasks with type s is denoted by N s , and randomly chosen in [1, M s ] • The total utilization U for each task set is randomly chosen in [1, s∈S M s /3]. • To ensure that the utilization of each type is not greater than the number of cores (which must not be scheduled), we allocate the utilization in proportion by the number of processors, i.e., U ×Ms a∈S Ma for each type s. • Using the UUnifast method [8] to allocate the U s to each task with type s (each single vertex task and one DAG task denoted as u s ). • For each single vertex task, the period is randomly chosen in [10,1000). And For the DAG task, we set 1000 as its period. Note that no single vertex task with a higher period than this DAG task. • the total WCET of each task is equal with U i × T i • This evaluation randomly generates 1000 task sets for each point of each experiment. We still use the method proposed in [9] to generate the the DAG structure, and use the same settings in [7] for the DAG task.

We compare the proposed method denoted by IMP-B with the known method called Base-B( which is presented in [6]) by acceptance ratio in different parameters. The acceptance ratio is defined as the ratio of the number of tasks that can be scheduled to the total number of tasks that are tested.

Figure 3(a)-(d) show the acceptance ratio experiment results. The experiment considers the influence of changing U , changing |V |, changing pr and changing |S|, respectively. In all these results, we can see that the acceptance ratio of IMP-B is much more precise than Base-B in the average situation. So, we claim that IMP-B is much more precise than Base-B under different parameter values.

Figure 4 shows the efficiency trends of the two methods. We can see that the |V | parameter affects the efficiency significantly. And under all parameters, the trends show that IMP-B needs more time than Base-B, but all are acceptable under the off-line analysis.

div.head: VI. RELATED WORK
div.p: The heterogeneous multi-core platform scheduling problem is mainly focused on scheduling different processor rates. The issue discussed in this paper restricts the available resources for parallel tasks, which is a resource restriction problem.

The resource restriction problem has been studied in the past, but the task model already studied is simple. [10], [11] studied the inclusive processing set restriction problem, and they only considered two tasks and two sets of cores. [12] studied a special processing restriction problem, which only considered two processing sets and they can overlap each other but one cannot be a subset to the other. [13] studied another processing set restrictions, which considered a processing set is denoted by a path of a tree. We can see that the problems discussed in these work differ from this paper. Otherwise, some work has been done on the scheduling problem of sequential tasks on heterogeneous multi-core platforms with resource restrictions [14], [15].

A particular case of the problem considered in this paper was studied in [17], [18]. In [18] studies the task with special structures, such as in-tree, out-tree, and so on. In [17], it assumes only two sets of cores, each task is chained, and each vertex of each task with unite WCET.

div.head: VII. CONCLUSION
div.p: This paper proposes a WCRT bound for typed DAG parallel tasks under higher priority tasks interfering on heterogeneous multi-cores. In this platform, each vertex of a DAG allows executing on the bounded cores. The already known methods of this task model are much more pessimistic. We propose a new WCRT bound for typed DAG tasks in this paper. The method we proposed in this paper could get the WCRT of a DAG task in polynomial time complexity. The simulation experiments show that our method greatly improves the precision of already known methods in a little consumption of efficiency. One direction of our future work is to expand highpriority tasks from single vertex to multiple vertex.
